harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent per-source SSH rate limiting on node1 for IPv4 and IPv6. Seven new connections per 60-second rolling window remain available; subsequent attempts are dropped. The policy survived firewall reload and node reboot, while normal SSH access remained healthy.
actions_performed: Added firewalld-managed IPv4 and IPv6 rules matching only new TCP/22 SYNs.
Kept established sessions and the normal SSH service allow rule unaffected.
Validated configuration reload and exercised the limiter through an isolated non-loopback source.
Restarted node1 safely and verified boot identity change, service recovery, rule persistence, and post-reboot limiter behavior.
Removed all temporary network test fixtures.

evidence.summary: Permanent configuration validated successfully, then identical runtime and kernel rules were present after firewalld reload.

evidence.requirement: Rate-limit repeated SSH connections while preserving normal access
evidence.summary: Post-reboot testing targeted node1's managed IP from an isolated source. Attempts 1–7 received OpenSSH banners; attempts 8–9 were dropped with firewall counters incrementing. A separate administrative source still received the OpenSSH banner.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Before reboot, boot ID was d9f8550d-5cb3-4929-9e62-a388df86bcf6 with healthy SSH/firewall services and loaded rules. The native reboot was acknowledged; afterward boot ID was d0612468-1c99-49f7-b10f-c8a9bbb3edbb, and sshd, firewalld, listeners, persistent rules, kernel rules, and the SSH banner all recovered.
System is running with sshd and firewalld active, two SSH listeners, four runtime and four permanent limiter rules, valid configuration, and no temporary namespace or veth remaining.
